2_Introduction: The inverted PSCs achieved a champion PCE of 25.1545% with an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.171 V, short-circuit current density (JSC) of 26.549 mA/cm², and fill factor (FF) of 80.9158%. The core perovskite solution, composed of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L, served as the foundational matrix for the solar cell. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively. 150 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 15 s before the end of the program. After the whole spin-coating process, the substrate was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The mixed-cation perovskite Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 leverages the complementary steric and electronic effects of its A-site constituents, where small Cs⁺ stabilizes the perovskite lattice, volatile MA⁺ facilitates rapid nucleation, and large FA⁺ optimizes the tolerance factor for phase stability and a favorable bandgap, while the high precursor concentration of 1.65 mol/L promotes a dense precursor film. The crystallization dynamics were precisely controlled by the two-stage spin-coating process; an initial 1000 rpm spread promotes uniform wetting, followed by a rapid 5500 rpm acceleration that induces supersaturation, with the timed introduction of 150 µL chlorobenzene antisolvent at 15 seconds before the spin end triggering rapid and homogeneous nucleation. This kinetic control suppresses the random formation of pinholes and minimizes the presence of unreacted PbI₂ intermediates, a process further consolidated by the subsequent 110 °C thermal annealing, which drives complete solvent evaporation, promotes oriented grain growth, and anneals out point defects, particularly on grain boundaries and at the perovskite surface, thereby reducing non-radiative recombination centers and enhancing charge carrier lifetimes. The resultant high-quality, pinhole-free film with large, uniformly oriented grains and a reduced defect density facilitates efficient charge extraction and transport, minimizing voltage losses and maximizing current collection, which collectively yielded the champion device performance with a VOC of 1.171 V, a JSC of 26.549 mA/cm², an FF of 80.9158%, and a PCE of 25.1545%.
